newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.86 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.86 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 80 basis points to 16.86 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 40 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 17.65 percent coupon for a price of 100.37 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 17.65 percent.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 18.03 percent coupon at a price of 99.04 percent and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 18.42 percent coupon at an average price of 98.54 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 127 basis points to 19.51 percent for the 269-day bills and 114 basis points to 20.19 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
